The edit-signature +6 is still not pinned to a commit, and nothing is committed or sent since the (2) bundle.

What the traces have shown so far:

- **What re-runs.** The +6 is all `law_findings`, on cache.av's five `use` items and its `impl` item. They re-run because their recorded read list includes `file_declares(cache.av)`. That answer carries every declaration's face, so any signature edit in the file moves it.
- **Where the read comes from.** When those items re-run, the current code never reads `file_declares` itself. The read most likely enters their read lists by replay: the engine records the reads made while a memo is worked out, then replays them to every later reader of that memo.
- **Ruled out:**
  - The entry_only commits (ed261dfa, c905744a) give exactly what the base56 merge they sit on gives.
  - Making `module_kept`, `module_winners` and `module_declares` cut queries changed nothing. The engine's check compares each read's whole answer, not the part a reader read, so the per-name split of the last two doesn't help. Fixing that is engine work in std-program, outside my lane.
  - `imports_refused`, added by ec9d036e, doesn't cut either, but it isn't on cache.av's path.

The next build traces replayed reads too and tags each with the law and the question it lands under. That should name the memo, and from it the commit to fix or name.

Still in the working tree, uncommitted:
- **Impl-undeclared cycle fix.** Its witness is red at bb4859f1; I'll show it green on the next clean build.
- **The three cut changes.** I'll revert them, since they bought nothing.
- **The temporary traces** in std-program and law_findings. I'll remove them before committing anything.

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 19 05:56:32 2026 +0000

    program layer: a file's `use` lines judged once, not once an item — the cold-build cost the import laws added
    
    - use_faults reads the `use` lines before an item only for an item that writes one: every other item paid a read of each item before it, nine laws over (O(items²) per file).
    - A clash asks what a module declares only where a line before binds the same name.
    - The names a file's `use` lines leave unbound are a query of the file (`imports_refused`): item_unknown_types, impls_untraited and unread_as asked them again for every item.
    - Cold `ir packages/cli`, summed over the bodies wave's cores: item_unknown_types 10.4 → 1.3 CPU-s; the import laws' own time falls from ~14 CPU-s to under 0.2.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, IN ITS WORDS, AND BUILDS WHAT IT BUILDS.
# Each case under tools/program-refusals/ is a package of its own:
#   refuses.expected — the source must be refused: the old path's `check` and the program
#     layer's `build` each exit 1, and what each says, its warnings aside, is exactly this text;
#   prints.expected — the source must not be refused: the old path's `check` exits 0, the
#     program layer builds it, and what the product prints is exactly this text;
#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers

db06_step5_witness.sh
queue-witness
tool_witnesses.sh

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.

AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \

# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}

payload.result:
<to_controller>
**(2) progress.** 8 of the 9 workspace_adversarial cases now pass. The cross-package re-export cycle is the one left, as you asked. There are 5 commits on avra-lane-parity-resolve-2 after 89575bfa, and each one unpins its own names from tools/gate/std-avrac.names:

- **c3221333 `use_meets_its_module` (resolve.import_clash), new law.** A `use` can't bind a name its own module already holds: the file's own declaration or the module's export. The words are the old path's: "`X` is imported, but this module (`main.av`) already has it". It unpins 3 cases: import shadowed by a local declaration, import of a name this file keeps apart, and an importer's own declaration of a re-exported name.
- **0e0b665b.** An `export use` claims its name for the module, so a sibling's private declaration clashes with it, in the same words. The surface law (reexport_twice) now counts only exported declarations. Unpins: "a re-export claims its name against a sibling's private declaration".
- **7a46e0ab.** A name the module declares twice is said once. reexport_twice and the new import law stay silent on it. `module_bindings` no longer records a declaration a second time when a re-export brings it back; before this, duplicate_in_module was said twice. Unpins: "a module that declares a name twice is refused once".
- **6ab32b08 `kept_apart_type` (resolve.kept_apart), new law.** A type that two sibling files each keep private, used in a third file's signature, is refused as kept apart instead of type.unknown. The words are the old path's `apart_read`. Unpins: "a kept-apart type named in a third file's signature".
- **bbaa5c9f: this one changes the test, not the law.** The layer already refuses the field-default and the method-clash cases in the right file. The tests failed only because a build judges the whole program, so the other file's `judged_at(..).clean()` saw that refusal too. Both tests now ask `said_in(file)`, the question they were written to ask. Overrule this if you'd rather the layer judge files one at a time.
- **Status.**

bbaa5c9f spec harness: a refusal said in its own file is asked where it stands — a build judges the whole program, so the field-default and method-clash attacks ask each file what is said in it
6ab32b08 resolve: a type two files of a module each keep private, named in a third file's signature, is refused as kept apart (resolve.kept_apart), not as naming no type
7a46e0ab resolve: a name its module declares twice is refused once — the re-export meeting it says nothing more, and a declaration a re-export brings back is no second clash
0e0b665b resolve: a re-export claims its name for its module, so a sibling's private declaration of it clashes (resolve.import_clash), and the surface law counts only what is on the surface
c3221333 resolve: a `use` binds no name its own module already holds — the file's own declaration or its module's export — said as the old path says it (resolve.import_clash: `X` is imported, but this module (`file`) already has it)
89575bfa formats: whether one format accepts every text another does is one function, @std/meta's `format_subsumes` — the compiler's `match` law and any library ask it — and an arm an earlier format arm covers is warned of (type.unreachable_arm)
4f0bbd35 formats: a hole reads its span as any type that crosses text — `string` and `int` by their identity, any other type through @std/text's `TextForm`: `from_text_form` in a match arm's scan and a grammar's `parse`, `text_form` in `print` and its round-trip guard
a1ef323f formats: a declared grammar's shape is a value — `R.parts()`, a fifth door beside `pattern()`, answers the prelude's `FormatShape` (its head, and each hole's name, type, greed and the literal after it), written from the format's own parts through one verb, `format_shape`
ffc89a85 program layer: a component word nobody imported, that a module of a package the manifests name exports, is told the `use` that brings it — at a parse that stops near it and at a record literal of it (`component_import`, one index a package, each file's words read once)
c9b4a5f0 program layer: a module's surface folds each re-export into what its files declare (`ModuleExports.with_shapes`), one literal

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, then the command the census compiler
# runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has the machine's store off, so
# its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds; `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's
# cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own price, ratcheted apart.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli off check --counts packages/cli
build-cli off build packages/cli
check-program off check --counts packages/std-program
cold-with-store-fill filled check --counts packages/cli

\`format_subsumes(a, b: FormatShape) -> Subsumed { Covers, Misses, Unknown }\` reads the scan's own rules:
- a \`b\` of no holes is one text, scanned by \`a\` (\`format_spans\`, each span read as its hole reads): exact;
- otherwise \`a\` covers where its holes stand where \`b\`'s do (one head, one piece and greed at each place), each reading at least what \`b\`'s reads (text anything, an \`int\` an \`int\`, a type crossing text only itself), or where \`a\` is one text hole between a prefix of \`b\`'s head and a suffix of \`b\`'s last piece;
- anything else is \`Unknown\`, never \`Misses\`, and warns nothing.
A hole's shape carries how it reads (\`HoleRead\`, from \`hole_reading\`'s identity), never its type's spelling. The law (\`arm_after_format\`, item_unreached.av) names the covering arm; the program layer's alone (differs.why). The witness harness's built programs carry the std prelude their \`@std/meta\` now reads (\`witness_host\`, one host for package and built witnesses). 1://! A FORMAT PATTERN'S SCAN: one anchored left-to-right pass over the subject's octets — the head a
2://! prefix, the last piece a suffix, and each piece between them found at its first place at or past
3://! the cursor, or its last where its hole is greedy. Nothing goes back, so the scan is linear in the
4://! subject, and a greedy hole may fail where its lazy twin would take: the place it took can leave a
5://! later piece unfound. Each step runs only where every step before it held, which keeps a cursor
6://! past the end from the search, whose start must stand inside. Each hole's span lands in cells the
7://! steps write; a value is cut from them only where an arm binds it. A hole that reads as an `int`
8://! reads its span once every span is found, still inside the verdict: a span that spells no `int`
9://! fails the scan, as a missing piece does, and the `int` lands in the hole's own cell.

# FORMATS — design note (B, then A, then C)

What exists today: `grammar R = "…"` is a record whose fields are its holes. On the layer its doors are
STATICS that item_formats.av generates as an `impl R { … }` from the record's `GrammarSpec { head, parts:
List<FormatPart { hole: Hole { name, ty: TypeRef?, greedy }, piece } }`. The four statics are `pattern`,
`parse`, `parse_octets` and `print`; the scan itself is the prelude's `format_spans`. On the old path the
same four are MethodRows (features/formats/mod.av). A pattern `"…"` in a `match` is `Pat.Format`,
read by the same reader (format.av `read_format`).

## B. `R.parts()` — a format's shape as a value

- **@std/meta declares the shape, once:** `FormatShape { head: string, holes: List<FormatHole> }` and
  `FormatHole { name: string, ty: string, greedy: bool, piece: string }`. `ty` is the type the hole
  binds, spelled as it is written: "string" where untyped.
- **The door is a fifth generated static,** `static fn parts() -> FormatShape`, beside `pattern()`.
  Its body is a record literal that item_formats writes from the same `GrammarSpec` it reads for
  `pattern()`. So it is read off the reader's parts, never re-parsed from the spelling, and no
  `crossing.av` row is needed: the value is static data the binary lays out like any const.
  `FORMAT_STATICS` gains "parts".
- **One definition:** the compiler converts `GrammarSpec → FormatShape` in exactly one verb,
  `format_shape(spec)`. B's door, C's library function and C's match law all read through it.
- **Old path:** the doors there are MethodRows. I'd give `parts` only to the layer and mark the gap
  (`tapes --new-only`), since the old path is being switched off. Say if you want the row as well.
- **Witness:** the README's wanted_door prints `3`, and `usage` drawn from `Copy.parts()` prints
  `<src:string> <dst:string...> <mode:int>`.

## A. A hole of any type that crosses as text

- **Today:** `reads_of(h)` matches `ty.name` against "string"/"int", the name-as-text dispatch
  CLAUDE.md forbids.
- **The decision moves to where the hole's type is RESOLVED.** Typing resolves the hole's `TypeRef`
  to a type and records a `HoleReading` fact per hole: `Text | Int | Form(ty)`.
  - `Text` and `Int` are told by the resolved type's identity (the owned `str`/`int`), not its spelling.
  - `Form(ty)` holds where `ty` implements `@std/text`'s `TextForm`. The trait is asked by DECLARED
    IDENTITY: on the layer the bound is the `SignedType` of the declaration `@std/text` exports
    (file + name), asked through `implements(engine, reader, ty, bound)` (item_methods.av, written
    impls first). On the old path it is the `DeclId` of that declaration through the impls table.
    No name is compared as text.
  - Anything else is refused once at the hole: "`T` crosses no text — implement `@std/text`'s
    `TextForm`" (type.format_parse, its voice re-worded to the law).
- **The readers take the fact, not the name:**
  - item_formats' `parse`: a `Form` hole is `T.from_text_form(span)?`, and absence fails the parse.
  - `print`: writes `r.f.text_form()`, and the round-trip guard (`survives`) runs on that same text.
  - A pattern arm (lower.av): binds through `T.from_text_form(span)`, and absence moves to the next arm.
  - `int` keeps its inline `format_int` path, and `string` its span.
- **One protocol a type:** parse and print both go through that type's `TextForm` impl; there is no
  registry and no second mechanism. `Time` works at once.
- **Witness:** the README's program prints `matched 7 miss 7 /items/i7`. A refusal case covers a hole
  typed by a type with no `TextForm`.

## C. `subsumes(A, B)` — "A accepts every text B accepts"

- **One definition, in @std/meta:** `export fn subsumes(a: FormatShape, b: FormatShape) -> Subsumed`,
  where `Subsumed { Covers, Misses, Unknown }`. It is pure Avra over B's value.
  - The compiler's match law calls it on `format_shape(spec)` of two arms.
  - `A.subsumes(B)` is a door that folds at compile time to `subsumes(A.parts(), B.parts()) ==
    .Covers`, so the compiler and every library ask the very same function.
- **Semantics, exactly the scan's:** a text matches F iff it begins with F's head and the scan
  succeeds. Hole k ends at its piece's FIRST occurrence (or its LAST where greedy), and a last piece
  "" means the hole takes the rest. Each span must also read as its type: `int` is `-?[0-9]+`,
  `string` is any text (empty included, as `format_spans` allows), and `Form(T)` is opaque.
- **The algorithm, where neither format holds a `Form` hole, is exact and decidable:**
  - Each such format denotes a REGULAR language.
    - A lazy hole followed by piece p is "a span holding no p, then p".
    - A greedy hole is "a span, then p, then a remainder holding no p".
    - Both are KMP automata over p.
  - The alphabet is partitioned into classes: each byte that occurs in either format's head or pieces,
    the digits, `-`, and "every other byte". The DFAs therefore stay small.
    - States per format are at most Σ|pieces| + |head| + (number of holes) × (KMP states of its piece).
  - "A covers B" is decided by emptiness of L(B) ∩ ¬L(A) on the product DFA, at most
    |DFA_A| × |DFA_B| states.
  - **The bound:** a cap of 4096 product states (the longest real route pattern gives well under 200).
    Past the cap it answers `Unknown`, and the walk itself is linear in the product.
- **A `Form(T)` hole is not regular.** Such a pair is decided only by STRUCTURAL ALIGNMENT:
  - Equal heads and equal pieces at each position.
  - Each of A's holes accepts at least what B's does at that position: `string` ⊇ everything,
    `int` ⊇ `int`, `Form(T)` ⊇ only `Form(T)`, the same type by identity.
  - Equal greed.
  - Alignment that holds is `Covers`; anything else is `Unknown`, never `Misses`. A `Form` hole can
    make no claim of missing.
- **Match reachability:**
  - In the layer's item_unreached, for each unguarded arm whose pattern is a format or a hole-free
    literal over a `string` subject, an earlier unguarded format arm `i` with
    `subsumes(i, j) == .Covers` warns `type.unreachable_arm` at arm j, naming arm i's pattern.
  - `Unknown` warns nothing.
  - A hole-free literal B needs no automaton: run A's scan on B's text, which is exact.
  - The README's three dead arms are each named. `{n: int}` over `{k: int}` is `Covers`: names don't
    matter, readings do.
- **std-http's `covers`/`shadows`** in route.av stay its own until it moves onto `subsumes`. Then there
  is no second copy; that is its owner's step, and I'd note it in the ROADMAP.
- **Old path:** it warns no format arm today. The new warnings are the layer's own (`tapes --new-only`
  doesn't apply to warnings), recorded as a known difference with its reason. Say if you'd rather the
  old path got the law too.

## Order and landing

- **B** comes first: it adds `FormatShape` and `format_shape`, which C's library function takes.
- **A** next: it adds `HoleReading`, and C reads the hole's reading through B's `ty`, plus the
  reading fact the match law needs.
- **C** last.
- Each is its own commit with its witnesses (prints cases, a refusal case for A, a warns case for C),
  and C's match law is witnessed in the README's three arms.
- **Questions for you:**
  1. The old-path doors for B and the old-path law for C, or layer-only?
  2. Is `@std/meta` the right home for `subsumes`, or a new `@std/formats`?

# One subsumption law over formats

**Commands** (from `engine_repros/`, compiler at avra-services `722523899`):

    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout 100 /Users/tristan/projects/tristanMatthias/avra-services/build/avra check format_subsumes
    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout 100 /Users/tristan/projects/tristanMatthias/avra-services/build/avra run format_subsumes
    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout 100 /Users/tristan/projects/tristanMatthias/avra-services/build/avra run format_subsumes/wanted_library

**Today:**
1. `check format_subsumes` exits 0 and prints nothing, no warning at all.
   `run` prints `id new id x n 3`. The arms `"/items/{slug}"`,
   `"/items/new"` and `"/pages/{k: int}"` are all dead: an earlier arm
   accepts every text they do.
2. A library cannot ask the question. `wanted_library` exits 1:

       error[type.unknown_prop]: `A` is a `grammar`, not an enum
       4 │ A.subsumes(B)
       help: `A.subsumes` is a call only where the grammar declares a door of that name

   The only implementation in the tree lives in one library, works on pattern
   TEXT, and runs at run time: `covers`, `open_hole` and `shadows` in
   std-http's `route.av`. It treats a TYPED hole as covering nothing but its
   own spelling. So `{n: int}` above `{k: int}` is reported as "equally
   specific … match some of the same targets", never as unreachable, although
   the two accept exactly the same texts.

**Wanted:**
1. `check format_subsumes` warns once per dead arm, in the shape of the
   existing `type.unreachable_arm`. The `/items/{slug}`, `/items/new` and
   `/pages/{k: int}` arms are each named, along with the earlier arm that
   covers them.
2. `A.subsumes(B)` answers `true`: a door on a declared grammar,
   compile-time foldable, over the same function.

**One definition:** a function over two formats' parts (core `FormatPart`).
- A covers B when the heads and pieces align.
- Each of A's holes accepts at least what B's hole at the same position
  accepts: untyped (`string`) accepts any text, `int` accepts `int`, a
  `TextForm` type accepts only itself. So two `int` holes cover each other
  whatever their names.
- Greed and the scan's first-occurrence rule are respected.
- The function answers "unknown" where it cannot prove coverage, and match
  reachability treats unknown as no warning.

Match reachability and the door both call it, so no second copy exists.

**Law:** an arm that an earlier arm subsumes never runs, and the compiler
says so with the same function a library calls.

**Second user:** a command-line subcommand table, or a log-line classifier
whose `match` over many line formats silently loses one when a broader
format is moved above it.
// (1) An earlier format arm that accepts everything a later arm accepts
// leaves the later arm dead, and nothing says so.
fn untyped(t: string) -> string {
    match t {
        "/items/{id}" -> "id ${id}",
        "/items/{slug}" -> "slug ${slug}",
        "/items/new" -> "new",
        _ -> "miss",
    }
}

// The typed case: two `int` holes under different names accept the same
// texts, so the second arm is dead too.
fn typed(t: string) -> string {
    match t {
        "/pages/{n: int}" -> "n ${n}",
        "/pages/{k: int}" -> "k ${k}",
        _ -> "miss",
    }
}

"${untyped("/items/new")} ${untyped("/items/x")} ${typed("/pages/3")}"
avra.toml
src
// (2) The wanted library question: does format A accept every text B does?
grammar A = "/items/{id}"
grammar B = "/items/new/{x}"
A.subsumes(B)

# A declared grammar's parts, as a value

**Command** (from `engine_repros/`, compiler at avra-services `722523899`):

    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout 100 /Users/tristan/projects/tristanMatthias/avra-services/build/avra run format_parts_as_value
    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout 100 /Users/tristan/projects/tristanMatthias/avra-services/build/avra run format_parts_as_value/wanted_door

**Today.** The first command exits 0. The library has only
`Copy.pattern()`, a string, so `holes_by_hand` re-implements the format
reader's rules. It does not handle `{{` escapes or malformed holes.

    copy {src} to {dst...}:{mode: int} => <src:string> <dst:string...> <mode:int>

The second command, asking for the parts directly, exits 1:

    error[type.unknown_prop]: `Copy` is a `grammar`, not an enum
      ╭─[…/wanted_door/src/main.av:3:1]
    3 │ Copy.parts().length
    help: `Copy.parts` is a call only where the grammar declares a door of that name

**What exists.** A grammar declares four doors (`features/formats/mod.av`):
`parse`, `parse_octets`, `print` and `pattern`. `pattern()` answers a
`string`. `@std/meta`'s `Format` is `{ node: Node }`, an opaque template
handle given only to a component's head field; it carries no parts either.
Compiler-side, the parts already exist as data: `GrammarSpec { head, parts:
List<FormatPart> }`, where each `FormatPart` is `{ hole: Hole { name, ty,
greedy }, piece }`. They just never cross to the program.

**Wanted:** a fifth door, `Copy.parts()`, returning a `@std/meta` value with
the head piece plus a list of `{ name, ty, greedy, piece }`. The second
command would then print `3`, and `usage` would read the parts instead of the
text. The record would cross through `crossing.av`'s rows like every other
meta shape, so the compiler's `Hole` and the library's view stay one
definition.

**Law:** a format's shape is read from the format, never re-parsed from its
spelling.

**Second user:** generated docs, or a CLI usage line
(`copy <src> to <dst...>:<mode:int>`) drawn from the same grammar that parses
the command.

#!/bin/sh
# tool-witness: --self-test
# BUILDS A LADDER: each rung's tree, in a worktree of its own, with the compiler of the rung before it, and
# answers the last product's path. The one definition CI's prepare and a lane's Sprite both call.
#
#   sh tools/ladder.sh <compiler> <rung-commit>...      prints the last rung's compiler on stdout
#   sh tools/ladder.sh --clean <dir>                    removes a ladder's scratch (its caller does, once it has copied the product)
#   sh tools/ladder.sh --self-test
#
# A rung's compiler is a REAL generation (`make avra` run by the previous rung's product), so each
# step is the one the generation law already asks of a tree, and a compiler is never asked to read
# what only a newer one can. A rung that does not build names itself and its log; nothing falls back
# to the seed, which cannot read a rung either. The whole ladder is capped at AVRA_LADDER_S (900 s),
# each rung at what is left. A ladder that FAILS removes its own scratch; one that builds leaves it for
# its caller, who copies the product and then asks `--clean`, so no ladder outlives its use.
#
# A RUNG IS REPLAYED ON THE TREE UNDER BUILD, NEVER ON ITS OWN. With AVRA_LADDER_BASE set (the base the
# tree is judged against: origin/main for a pull request, the commit before for main's own push), the
# rung's tree is that base with the rung merged in — what a batch or a squash makes of it — so a rung
# whose branch began before the base moved is read with the base's sources, not its stale ones. A rung
# the base already holds is no rung: the starting compiler, built from the base, already reads it.
set -eu
# a compiler is replaced here by the build it just ran, so each build saves its store before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
# A ladder's scratch: each rung's worktree (registered in the repository) and its logs, all gone.
ladder_clean() {
    [ -d "$1" ] || return 0
    for w in "$1"/rung-*; do
        [ -d "$w" ] && git worktree remove --force "$w" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
    done
    find "$1" -delete 2>/dev/null || :
    git worktree prune >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}
if [ "${1:-}" = --clean ]; then
    ladder_clean "${2:?usage: ladder.sh --clean <dir>}"
    exit 0
fi
if [ "${1:-}" = --self-test ]; then
    me=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/$(basename "$0")
    d=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-ladder.XXXXXX")
    git init -q -b main "$d/repo"
    g() { git -C "$d/repo" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t "$@"; }
    # a tree whose `make avra` copies the compiler it is handed, stamped with the rung it built
    cat > "$d/repo/Makefile" <<'MK'
avra:
	@mkdir -p build
	@{ cat build/avra; echo "built-by-previous"; } > build/avra.next && chmod +x build/avra.next && mv build/avra.next build/avra
MK
    echo one > "$d/repo/rung"; g add -A; g commit -q -m "rung one

Rung: one"
    r1=$(g rev-parse HEAD)
    echo two > "$d/repo/rung"; g commit -q -am "rung two

Rung: two"
    r2=$(g rev-parse HEAD)
    printf '#!/bin/sh\nstart\n' > "$d/start"; chmod +x "$d/start"
    out=$(cd "$d/repo" && AVRA_LADDER_DIR="$d/work" sh "$me" "$d/start" "$r1" "$r2" 2>"$d/err") || { cat "$d/err"; echo "ladder: a two-rung ladder failed"; exit 1; }
    [ -x "$out" ] && [ "$(grep -c built-by-previous "$out")" = 2 ] \
        || { echo "ladder: the product was not built twice in a chain: $out"; exit 1; }

d268367d compiler: a compile-time run on the program layer is held to its declaring package's `[lifted]` rows
A generator, an annotation seat's settled default and an instance check ran under the default
budgets alone, while a const asked the package that declares it; every compile-time run now asks
`lifted_budgets` of the package whose declaration it runs over.

Rung: a package's `[lifted]` row raises a derive only under a compiler that reads it

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJuoshSWsdEfYE13QV23

b4d9e59b runtime: a box's frame is the cell marked as one
A cell's mark byte gains MARK_FRAME: the cell is the frame of contexts
its box was made or placed under. avra_ctx_frame_pushed pushes the frame
in force onto a box with that mark, and avra_ctx_reframed replaces a cell
only where it wears it; any other box, a closure that carries no frame
among them, is answered as it is. A copy keeps the mark. The compiler
names each mark bit once (core/runtime_api.av's cell marks), the backend
lays static boxes' marks from them, and the generated header asserts
each is runtime/avra_box.h's. The new row reaches the world, as the
other context rows do.

Rung: the row exists before the evaluator arms it or the lowering pushes a frame with it

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01F8zAGduwLdaehWEhgee7MP

1e0d5d1c runtime: a strided list — each element its words in place, read in elements
A list whose element is several words — a flat record of scalars — lays each element's `k` words
in place: its length counts words, its element count is that over `k`. The rows that only move
words (push, concat, extend, grow, clone, reclaim) need no stride; five rows answer in ELEMENTS
and take `k` from the site, which knows its element type:

- avra_stride_len: the element count.
- avra_stride_at: element `i`'s first word, bounds-checked in elements, so a trap says the
  program's own index and length.
- avra_stride_last: where the last element's words begin, the list as it was; a pop reads them,
  then takes the words off with the word row, so every read is of a word the list still holds —
  in the evaluator as natively.
- avra_stride_slice and its _reusing twin: clamped in ELEMENTS before the bounds are words, so no
  bound a program writes overflows the multiply.

1e0d5d1c runtime: a strided list — each element its words in place, read in elements
A list whose element is several words — a flat record of scalars — lays each element's `k` words
in place: its length counts words, its element count is that over `k`. The rows that only move
words (push, concat, extend, grow, clone, reclaim) need no stride; five rows answer in ELEMENTS
and take `k` from the site, which knows its element type:

- avra_stride_len: the element count.
- avra_stride_at: element `i`'s first word, bounds-checked in elements, so a trap says the
  program's own index and length.
- avra_stride_last: where the last element's words begin, the list as it was; a pop reads them,
  then takes the words off with the word row, so every read is of a word the list still holds —
  in the evaluator as natively.
- avra_stride_slice and its _reusing twin: clamped in ELEMENTS before the bounds are words, so no
  bound a program writes overflows the multiply.

    program layer: an annotation names fields of the record it stands on, by seats of @std/meta's Field
    
    A seat of `@std/meta`'s `Field`, or a rest seat of a list of them, past a first seat taking the
    declaration's `Type`, takes the words written there as names of the annotated record's fields: a
    word is read among its fields, never as an expression, and crosses as that field's whole `Field`.
    A word naming no field is refused at the word with the field it's nearest offered; an argument
    that is no bare word, an annotation naming fields on a declaration with none, and a fn whose first
    seat takes no `Type` beside a `Field` seat are refused. Only the program layer builds the form,
    so the net steps aside for a program using it.

On a TYPE, an annotation's positional arguments are read as the type's own fields, but a
named argument's value is resolved as an ordinary name. So `@tag(lane, absent: done_at)`

# A type-level annotation's NAMED argument is resolved as an expression

Compiler: batch-55 macOS binary, run from /Users/tristan/projects/tristanMatthias/avra-services
(branch `services`, HEAD 82040a20c), one command at a time.

## Finding

On a TYPE, an annotation's positional arguments are read as the type's own fields, but a
named argument's value is resolved as an ordinary name. So `@tag(lane, absent: done_at)`
is `resolve.unresolved` ("`done_at` is not defined"). The annotation still runs, and
`Annotation.named` still holds `absent=done_at`. The same named argument as a FIELD mark,
`@tag(absent: done_at) lane`, is not resolved and is not refused. std-db is not needed.

# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {
    cold cli
    find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete
    c0=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-cold" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    c1=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-warm" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    echo "cli build net $1: cold $((c1 - c0))s, warm $(( $(date +%s) - c1 ))s" >>"$out/seconds"
    # the warm build's heir waited out, before a row after empties the store it saves
    env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}

slice_build() {
    row try make try
    row avra-a make avra && cp build/avra "$out/avra-a"
    cold cli
    row avra-b make avra && { cmp -s build/avra "$out/avra-a"; judged fixed-point $?; }
    cli_built on 1
    cli_built off 0
    judged cli-build-false-refusals "$(cat "$out"/cli-build-*.log | grep -c 'program-layer false refusal')"
}

# the std-avrac suite over `$@`, its paths under the package: one row for every path of std-avrac's
# own, and a row each for a path that is a package of its own nested in it, which `test` proves apart
avrac() {
    cold std-avrac
    own=""
    for p in "$@"; do
        if [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ]; then tested "std-avrac-$(basename "$p")" "$p"; else own="$own $p"; fi
    done
    [ -z "$own" ] || tested std-avrac $own
}
# half of std-avrac's src/compiler/tests, the `$1`-th (from 0), dealt in turn
compiler_tests_half() { find packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name '.*' | sort | dealt "$1" 2; }

// proves: a value boxed into a `dyn` seat implements the seat's trait by an impl a generator made$
// for a type other than the one the generator stands on M-bM-^@M-^T `collect enum Shape: Size` writes$
// `impl Size for Shape` on an enum no annotation marks M-bM-^@M-^T and the seat takes it$
use @std.meta.{Named}$
$
fn numbered(what: Named, ordinal: int) -> void {}$
$
trait Size {$
    fn size() -> int$
}$
$
@numbered(0)$
type Dot = {}$
$
impl Size for Dot {$
    fn size() -> int { 1 }$
}$
$
@numbered(1)$
type Line = { from: int }$
$
impl Size for Line {$
    fn size() -> int { self.from }$
}$
$
collect enum Shape: Size = @numbered in self by it.mark.args[0] dense$
$
fn total(xs: List<dyn Size>) -> int { xs.fold(0, (a, s) -> a + s.size()) }$
$
println("${total([Shape.Dot, Shape.Line(5)])}")$

#!/bin/sh
# THE CHANGED-FILE FMT CHECK — ONE definition, called by the gate's own fmt
# step (.github/workflows/checks.yml) and by `tools/work land`'s local
# preflight, so the two can never drift into two instruments.
#
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>     # the caller has refs (the gate)
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh --files <files…>  # the caller already diffed
#
# Every named `.av` file is run through `fmt --check`. The compiler is
# `${AVRA:-build/avra}` — the tree under test's OWN build. THE BRANCH'S
# COMPILER, NEVER A STALE STANDING ONE: a binary that predates the syntax a
# branch added REFUSES that branch's files and cannot report the canonical
# diff, so it would certify a file the gate then refuses. The gate has its
# own build; a lane's Sprite holds a branch build (`tools/work run`), and its
# synced tree carries no `.git`, which is why `--files` exists. Nothing
# here polls `main`: the refs are named, never watched.
set -eu
[ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head> | --files <files…>" >&2; exit 2; }
avra=${AVRA:-build/avra}
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 2; }

# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0

OLD_PATH=${GATE_OLD_PATH:-1}
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
ROW_SECS=${GATE_ROW_SECS:-2400}
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
# the packages whose tests the doors slices run

DOORS_B="std-ui std-http"

slices() {
    cat <<'EOF'
build      make try; make avra twice, the second cold, the two binaries one; cli build cold+warm, net on and off, 0 false refusals
avrac-a    test packages/std-avrac — half of src/compiler/tests, dealt in turn, and every dir of src/compiler but tests and soundness

idioms-avrac  check --baseline tools/idioms.baseline on std-avrac, when the diff from <base> touches it

doors-b    test std-ui std-http; make ui-host-test and ui-host, std-ui's program tests built and run
findings-a tapes --findings on std-avrac and cli, 0 refusals; std-avrac built, 0 program-layer false refusals
findings-b the same on a third of every other package, dealt in turn
findings-c the next third
findings-d the last third
refusal-a  witness_program_refusal over a third of its cases, dealt in turn
refusal-b  the next third
refusal-c  the last third
witness-b  witness_program_runs, heir_save_attack, share_merge_attack, wave_share_attack, beside_attack, _ledger, _suites, _doors; witness_program_differential; make flow-trace; witness_compiler_key; docs_cache_attack, obj_gone_attack, moved_tree_attack, layer_sites_attack, closure_gather_attack, store_bound_attack, path_leak_attack, case_leftover_attack, witness_program_fixes, root_listing_attack, two_compilers_attack

warnings-b witness_program_warnings — the cli's check on both paths, and the cases under tools/program-warnings/
warnings-c witness_program_warnings — the cli edited, built warm on the program layer

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, IN ITS WORDS, AND BUILDS WHAT IT BUILDS.
# Each case under tools/program-refusals/ is a package of its own:
#   refuses.expected — the source must be refused: the old path's `check` and the program
#     layer's `build` each exit 1, and what each says, its warnings aside, is exactly this text;
#   prints.expected — the source must not be refused: the old path's `check` exits 0, the
#     program layer builds it, and what the product prints is exactly this text;
#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cases_dir="$root/tools/program-refusals"
# the node a wasm case's module runs under: NODE, else /opt/node24's, else the PATH's
node=${NODE:-$( [ -x /opt/node24/bin/node ] && echo /opt/node24/bin/node || echo node )}

. "$root/tools/lib/cases.sh"
# every case, by name
cases() { cases_in "$cases_dir"; }

if [ "${1:-}" = --cases ]; then
    cases
    exit 0
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = --known ]; then
    n=0
    for name in $(cases); do
        [ -e "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why" ] || continue
        echo "$name: $(head -1 "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why")"
        n=$((n + 1))
    done
    echo "witness_program_refusal: $n of $(cases | wc -l | tr -d ' ') cases known to differ"
    exit 0
fi
avra=${1:-build/avra-try}
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_refusal: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
48:avrac-a    test packages/std-avrac — half of src/compiler/tests, dealt in turn, and every dir of src/compiler but tests and soundness
49:avrac-g    test packages/std-avrac — the other half of src/compiler/tests, and src/compiler/soundness
50:avrac-b    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[a-e]*
51:avrac-c    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[f-m]*
52:avrac-d    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[n-r]*
53:avrac-e    test packages/std-avrac — src/features/[s-z]*
54:avrac-f    test packages/std-avrac — src/features' own files, and every dir of src/ but compiler and features
226:        if [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ]; then tested "std-avrac-$(basename "$p")" "$p"; else own="$own $p"; fi
427:        avrac-a) slice_avrac_a ;;
428:        avrac-b) slice_avrac_b ;;
429:        avrac-c) slice_avrac_c ;;
430:        avrac-g) slice_avrac_g ;;
431:        avrac-d) slice_avrac_d ;;
432:        avrac-e) slice_avrac_e ;;
433:        avrac-f) slice_avrac_f ;;

# HANDOFF — avra-lane-parity-resolve-2

## Lane and scope
- **Lane:** avra-lane-parity-resolve-2, the Avra compiler's program layer.
- **Goal:** the program layer (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0) says what the old path (AVRA_PROGRAM=0) says: kind, words, place and count.
- **My families:** resolve.* (imports, re-exports, scope), plus laws routed to me by the lead.
- **Rules (LANE_BRIEF):**
  - one definition per law;
  - no `rm` (use `find … -delete`), no `git stash`, no `reset --hard`, no `--no-verify`;
  - push nowhere; commit as you go;
  - run fmt --write on every .av you touch;
  - one heavy build at a time;
  - post to the lead only at a bundle, a blocker or a ruling.
- **Lead contact:** the claude-bridge tools `post_to_controller` and `send_files`. The session token was in the bridge note; a new session gets its own.

## Base
- **Repo:** /work/avra, branch `avra-lane-parity-resolve-2`, HEAD 324fd3c59.
- **Landed:** everything through 7e717b29 (my merge of batch52 572c1d99) was sent and landed as batch 52's first merge.
- **batch53:** d5062c32, local ref `batch53`, which I hold. My lane is NOT merged onto batch53. Commit c0493354 (= ec9d036e cherry-picked) was sent ON batch53 as one commit and is gating in batch 53.
- **lane.bundle** = `avra-lane-parity-resolve-2 ^d750dfa70`.
- **Working tree:** clean; uncommitted.patch is empty.

## Commits ahead of the last landed bundle (7e717b29), not yet sent as a lane bundle
- 5cebcb116: a named top-level instance is a declaration (ruled). Built once through the once slot, readable by name from any fn, exported/imported like a declaration. The entry builds it where written (`runs_in_entry`); a module file builds it lazily. Also:
  - the layer's instance unit is `once` (fixes a wrong answer: an exported instance was rebuilt at every read);
  - `let`→`const` fix on resolve.runtime_binding (Remedy.Fix, High; `let_made_const`, `const_fix`, `made_const`; `FoundFix.item`);
  - instance builds and untyped un-typable consts are checked as bodies;
  - const.cycle widened to builds (`build_reads_itself_law`).
- c226844e4: witnesses for the above, the std-queue services_shape program test, and migrated programs. The std-queue tests flow07_failure_dead, flow07_handler_acks, home_refuses and typed_dead now use typed `state` channels/cells; event_holder and children_named changed too.
- 97a803d37: one `check` judgement per declared instance on the layer. The old path builds every declared instance at run time (dropped `settles`). Three component tests move to the ruling.
- ad8e9daab: differs.why texts. Cycle cases: the old path recurses at run time. handler_assigns_capture: two voices.
- ec9d036ea: COST FIX. A file's `use` lines are judged once (an item without `use` lines returns early; clash pre-filter; `imports_refused` file query). Cold law_findings 40.8→23.0, item_unknown_types 10.6→1.2 CPU-s. ALSO SENT as c0493354 on batch53.
- fee7b8a7b: COST/soundness. `implements` asks written impls first and generated ones only if none answers. Witness builds_dyn_over_collect_enum. The earlier annotated-only shortcut was UNSOUND (collect enum, @delegates), now replaced.
- c35746831: resolver loop fix. A name a module's `use` line binds (exported or not) is no generator's (`imports_name` in item_scope.av; `reexports_name` kept for other laws). Fixes importing `Loc` into testing/held.av looping file_scope↔package_impls.
- ce6bd57f0: witness import_of_a_private_import.
- 324fd3c59: a module's own declaration re-exported by a sibling file of the same module is no duplicate (`if prior.is(d) { continue }` in `module_bindings`). Witness builds_reexport_of_a_sibling. The component test now uses `refused_in(built(…))`.

## In flight when stopped
- **Receipts at ce6bd57f** (before 324fd3c5):
  - gates a, c–g PASS; check std-avrac exit 0; cli exit 0; idioms 0 NEW;
  - fmt: 2 differing, both batch52's own hunks in item_context.av and features/contexts.av, not mine;
  - avrac-b had 1 failure, my component test using the wrong helper, fixed in 324fd3c5;
  - the witness run then died: disk full.
- **Rerun at 324fd3c5** (full witness + avrac-b, background) was in progress, result unknown. NEXT: rerun `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try` and `sh tools/gate.sh avrac-b`, then the full receipts (handoff/scripts/gates.sh), then bundle `batch52..HEAD` (or merge batch53 first if the lead says so) and send.

## Next 3 items, in order
1. **Finish receipts and send the lane bundle** (all commits above). Merge onto batch53 if the lead asks (c0493354 is already in it; drop or skip the duplicate ec9d036e).
2. **(a) entry_only judges every module file, reached or not.** A whole-package `check` passes a module file that runs statements when the program doesn't reach it. Sits next to `runs_in_entry` / `strays_of` (item_program.av:853) and the old path's `entry_only` (lower.av).
3. **(b) Component import remedy on the layer.** "add this `use`" (`use @acme.kit.{c3}`) exists only on the old path; parse_refusal_test pins it. Search the program's packages by name, bounded, each file read at most once per lookup.

Also queued earlier, still pending:
- type.catch: `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block. The layer builds it unjudged; native LLVM PHI crash, a P0. Old voice `arm_not_ok`; subset case compiler/tests/subset/refusals_test.av:307.
- workspace_adversarial_test 11 pins, entry_only pair first.
- Generated-bodies measurement table: the lead's step 1. Branch `measure-generated` in /work/dev is stale; redo on the current HEAD with `judged_count`.
- `let xs = []; xs.map(it)` is silent on the layer.

## Open rulings / asks waiting on others
- **Lone-file prelude question:** held for the owner's ruling.
- **Remaining law cost** (context_set_before_read, arity_mismatch, declaration_warning_at_use, bitwise_mixed_law, alias_copy_held, ~0.3–0.5 s each): the lead is routing them to their lanes.

- **item_instances_checked own row** (lead's 1.1→14.2): I couldn't show it with the 15-row timing. I offered an instrumented build or parallel-main's bodies_wave.sh.

## Known gaps found, not fixed
- An untyped `state` whose start is a generic call has no type on the layer; instance builds reading it don't lower ("an untyped `const`"). Workaround: write the type.
- On the old path, a build that reads itself has no law: it recurses at run time (the three cycle cases carry differs.why). Since 97a803d3 the old path builds declared instances at run time, like the layer.

## Things a fresh session would trip on
- **A build reads the std packages beside the HOST binary.** Building a worktree with `AVRA_BIN=/work/avra/build/avra-try` compiles /work/avra/packages, not the worktree's. Copy the host into `<worktree>/build/avra` and run `make try` there with no AVRA_BIN.
- **Builds:**
  - `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12000 AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000 AVRA_PROGRAM=0 make try` builds build/avra-try (~25 min);
  - the gate's gen1 uses build/avra;
  - NEVER edit sources while a build or the gates run: they read sources mid-run, and I lost runs that way.
- **Disk:** the session's allowance fills fast. Each cold copy's `.avra-cache` is several GB, and the witness died on a full disk. Clean /tmp/claude-0/cold and old worktrees' `.avra-cache` (/work/base, /work/snap: caches already cleared).
- **Old path:** it can't check packages/std-avrac any more (`ctx` is layer-only). Use NET=0 layer checks there.

  - gates.sh: check, slices a..g, cli, witness, idioms;
  - gates52.sh: no witness/cli;
  - coldtapes.sh: cold `ir packages/cli --time`;
  - coldtapes_findings.sh: cold `tapes packages/cli --findings`;
  - hunk.py / union.py: diff3 conflict helpers.
- **Kept binaries:**
  - /work/avra/build/avra-try: HEAD-ish (built at 324fd3c5);

# Cloud lanes — how we use Claude Code web sandboxes

One lane = one cloud session = one sandbox = one branch. The lead (local Mac session) coordinates through the
`claude-web` bridge (`../claude_web_mcp`, README there is the tool reference).

## Names — one id everywhere

The bridge makes the name: `create_session {project: "avra", kind: "lane"|"ops", topic}` -> `avra-lane-<topic>`
(a taken name gets `-2`, `-3`). It sets the title and tells the agent its branch and file stem; nobody types a name.

| Where | Spelling |
|---|---|
| Cloud session title | `avra-lane-<topic>` |
| Git branch | `avra-lane-<topic>` |
| Bundle a lane hands back | `avra-lane-<topic>.bundle` |
| Lane note | `.lead/handoff/avra-lane-<topic>.md` |
| Non-lane sessions (builds, probes) | `avra-ops-<what>` |

## What a sandbox is

- Environment **Avra 2**: Ubuntu 24.04, 4 cores, 15 GB, no swap, 30 GB disk, ~2 min to start.
- Setup script leaves: LLVM 22, a built Linux compiler in `/opt/avra-tc`, the source at `/work/avra`
  (artifact `avra-work.tar.gz`: a shallow clone of `program` and open lane branches, ~150 MB — keep it small, a 290 MB download failed), lead notes at `/work/lead`, the bridge runner started.
- Suspended ~9 min after its agent's turn ends; disk survives, processes do not. A lane keeps its turn open
  while a job runs; the bridge hook restarts the runner on resume.
- No shared pool, no shared disk: a lane may run the whole gate by itself.

## The loop

1. Lead: `create_session` in "Avra 2" with `project`, `topic` and the brief (goal, files,
   what is ruled out, checks to run, how to report).
2. Lane: `cd /work/avra && git checkout -b avra-lane-<topic> program`, build with `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 make try`
   (~1.5 min), work, commit as it goes.
3. Lane self-gates in its sandbox: new-path `make try`, its own tests, `tapes --built`, the suites it touched,
   `tools/witness_program_edit.sh`. Reports exact counts with `post_to_controller`.
4. Lane hands back: `git bundle create /work/avra-lane-<topic>.bundle program..avra-lane-<topic>` and sends
   it (`send_files`). Nothing is pushed to GitHub.
5. Lead: fetch the bundle into `../avra-ho-land`, merge, run the Mac gate once per batch, move `program`,
   refresh the `avra-work.tar.gz` artifact (and the Linux compiler artifact when codegen moved).
6. Lane rebases onto the new `program` (fetch the artifact bundle) and takes its next item.

## Lead's direct door (no model in the loop)

`bun src/cli.ts exec <cse> [--cwd D --timeout S --wait S --bg] -- <cmd>` runs a command in a sandbox in ~1 s.
Use it for builds, gate runs and file pulls; use `send_message` only for judgement work.

## Rules

- Never push to main; lanes push nowhere. Hand-back is a bundle through the bridge.
- A lane touches only its own branch. Two lanes never own one file set — the brief names the files.
- Speed claims: exact counts plus `cmp` of products on one fixed source.
- Credentials in a sandbox's environment are never printed, posted or forwarded.
- The Mac gate is the bar for moving `program`; a cloud gate is the lane's own proof.

## Capacity

Each sandbox is its own machine, so lanes no longer compete for the Mac's memory or disk. The limit is the
lead's landing rate (one Mac gate per batch, merges serial), so lanes are cut by file ownership and landed in
batches.

# Cloud lanes — how we use Claude Code web sandboxes

One lane = one cloud session = one sandbox = one branch. The lead (local Mac session) coordinates through the
`claude-web` bridge (`../claude_web_mcp`, README there is the tool reference).

## Names — one id everywhere

The bridge makes the name: `create_session {project: "avra", kind: "lane"|"ops", topic}` -> `avra-lane-<topic>`
(a taken name gets `-2`, `-3`). It sets the title and tells the agent its branch and file stem; nobody types a name.

| Where | Spelling |
|---|---|
| Cloud session title | `avra-lane-<topic>` |
| Git branch | `avra-lane-<topic>` |
| Bundle a lane hands back | `avra-lane-<topic>.bundle` |
| Lane note | `.lead/handoff/avra-lane-<topic>.md` |
| Non-lane sessions (builds, probes) | `avra-ops-<what>` |

## What a sandbox is

- Environment **Avra 2**: Ubuntu 24.04, 4 cores, 15 GB, no swap, 30 GB disk, ~2 min to start.
- Setup script leaves: LLVM 22, a built Linux compiler in `/opt/avra-tc`, the source at `/work/avra`
  (artifact `avra-work.tar.gz`: a shallow clone of `program` and open lane branches, ~150 MB — keep it small, a 290 MB download failed), lead notes at `/work/lead`, the bridge runner started.
- Suspended ~9 min after its agent's turn ends; disk survives, processes do not. A lane keeps its turn open
  while a job runs; the bridge hook restarts the runner on resume.
- No shared pool, no shared disk: a lane may run the whole gate by itself.

## The loop

1. Lead: `create_session` in "Avra 2" with `project`, `topic` and the brief (goal, files,
   what is ruled out, checks to run, how to report).
2. Lane: `cd /work/avra && git checkout -b avra-lane-<topic> program`, build with `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 make try`
   (~1.5 min), work, commit as it goes.
3. Lane self-gates in its sandbox: new-path `make try`, its own tests, `tapes --built`, the suites it touched,
   `tools/witness_program_edit.sh`. Reports exact counts with `post_to_controller`.
4. Lane hands back: `git bundle create /work/avra-lane-<topic>.bundle program..avra-lane-<topic>` and sends
   it (`send_files`). Nothing is pushed to GitHub.
5. Lead: fetch the bundle into `../avra-ho-land`, merge, run the Mac gate once per batch, move `program`,
   refresh the `avra-work.tar.gz` artifact (and the Linux compiler artifact when codegen moved).
6. Lane rebases onto the new `program` (fetch the artifact bundle) and takes its next item.

## Lead's direct door (no model in the loop)

`bun src/cli.ts exec <cse> [--cwd D --timeout S --wait S --bg] -- <cmd>` runs a command in a sandbox in ~1 s.
Use it for builds, gate runs and file pulls; use `send_message` only for judgement work.

## Rules

- Never push to main; lanes push nowhere. Hand-back is a bundle through the bridge.
- A lane touches only its own branch. Two lanes never own one file set — the brief names the files.
- Speed claims: exact counts plus `cmp` of products on one fixed source.
- Credentials in a sandbox's environment are never printed, posted or forwarded.
- The Mac gate is the bar for moving `program`; a cloud gate is the lane's own proof.

## Capacity

Each sandbox is its own machine, so lanes no longer compete for the Mac's memory or disk. The limit is the
lead's landing rate (one Mac gate per batch, merges serial), so lanes are cut by file ownership and landed in
batches.

DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.

## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
  standard signature and is not a verb.
- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
  the category.
- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.

## Dogfooding is design

The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.

## Rules

- `core/` is infrastructure only. Features never import features.
- Layering is one-way: core -> grammar -> features -> compiler, all
  over `@std/relation`, whose `engine/` is the memo kernel —
  infrastructure, language-agnostic, the one a running program asks too.
  `grammar/` is the language-agnostic engine; `compiler/` is the
  driver and the ONE definition of Avra (feature order is branch
  order is the language).
- No string tags or string-matching to detect behavior.
- `_ ->` over our own enums is decided by COUNTING THE ANSWERING
  ARMS. One arm answers -> a PROJECTION, and the catch-all is
  honest: its contract pins the answer for variants that do not
  exist yet. TWO OR MORE answer -> a REGISTRY, and a catch-all there
  silently forgets the next variant (`let_name` dropped For's
  counter exactly so; `type_decl_name` would have swallowed the next
  type-declaring statement). Registries spell every arm — `or`-runs
  keep that affordable. Ratcheted as style.registry_catchall AND held by the compiler:
  F2040 counts the ANSWERING ARMS over the declared enum and names
  the variants a hole would forget. The license is a SPELLING, not a
  comment — `rest ->` says the remainder is deliberate, and both the
  compiler and the ratchet read it. The two licensed shapes are a
  feature matching its own variants (it cannot enumerate other
  features') and a loop that DELEGATES the rest to an exhaustive
  dispatch — each writes `rest ->` at the site.
  AND THE LAW IS ABOUT THE TEST, NOT THE MATCH. For a REGISTRY enum
  `is .Variant` IS A CATCH-ALL IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES: a boolean that
  asks about ONE variant and falls through for the rest discharges
  the registry's obligation no better than `_ ->`, and it is harder
  to see. For a PROJECTION enum it stays the right idiom. Two
  `RtKind` consumers were written that way (`rt_arg`, `answers_word`
  in llvm.av), correct only while the enum had three variants —
  widening it to carry C's integer widths would have sent an Avra
  `int` into an `i32` seat with no truncation, compiling clean. Both
  are exhaustive matches now.
  ENFORCEMENT SPLITS FROM THE LAW HERE, deliberately: no grep tells a
  registry enum from a projection one, so this gets NO ratchet rule.
  The keeper is `make vocab`, a CURATED table naming each registry's
  consumers and refusing BOTH shapes inside them — the table says
  which registries it holds, and a registry it does not name is
  unguarded. Naming the next one IS how this law is enforced.
  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES INTO C, where no keeper can follow. The
  runtime's `acc_kind_of` was a kind-keyed ternary falling through to
  ACC_RECORD — correct for the three kinds that existed when it was
  written and wrong from that same day for `KIND_STATIC`, so every
  immortal string was filed as a RECORD by `AVRA_MEM_STATS`: the
  instrument THIS FILE names as the way to answer a memory question,
  miscounting its own data since birth. A C chain keyed on our kinds
  carries a registry's obligation and `make vocab` cannot see it, so
  spell the kinds there too.
  AND THE REASON IT HID GENERALIZES: `RtKind` had three variants from
  the day it was written and had not yet grown — it carries six now
  — so nothing ever tested the assumption. A KEEPER THAT HAS ONLY
  EVER GUARDED A STATIC ENUM IS UNTESTED — the first widening is its
  first real test, and that is the worst moment to learn it was only
  ever looking for one shape.
  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES A PACKAGE BOUNDARY TOO, not only into C.
  A registry keyed on ANOTHER PACKAGE'S enum is spelled over NAMES —
  `node_value` matches `@std.meta.Node`'s variant names, because a
  foreign enum has no typed id here — so no compiler law and no grep
  sees it, and its `_ -> null` forgot the next variant the way every
  registry hole does: a template generated nothing and nobody was
  told. The keeper cannot follow across the seam; spell the arms and
  make the unknown SPEAK.
- THE EXEMPTION LAW, which the above is one instance of: a doctrine
  exemption that is not written AT THE SITE is an unbounded amnesty.
  Prose exemptions are invisible to tooling and to the next reader,
  so they rot into the default. Every licensed deviation carries
  `// LICENSED I<n>: <reason>` where the code is — that is what
  makes `make idioms` able to demand a decision instead of guessing
  which deviations were once approved.
- Node facts (spans included) live in side tables keyed by typed ids,
  never on nodes.
- A SLOT'S SEED IS COMPUTED THE SAME WAY AS ITS UPDATES, or the
  first decision judges a different quantity from every later one —
  and only the first, which is what makes it invisible.
  `collapse_breaks` seeded `line_indent` from `raw[0].span.lo`, a
  byte OFFSET, and assigned it a character DISTANCE everywhere after;
  the seed read as a column only while the first token sat on line
  one, so a LEADING COMMENT's own length became the indent and a
  four-character comment changed how the file parsed. Write the seed
  as the update's rule applied to nothing, not as whatever value
  happens to be at hand.
- A fact EVERY BODY MAY READ is answered from the PROGRAM — the
  store — never from a pass's fact tables. Fact tables are per
  declaration, over that declaration's expression range alone, so an
  answer computed from `facts` is right in the body that recorded it
  and WRONG everywhere else (a const's declared `int?` read back as
  `int` across a fn floor, and `??` warned it would never fire).
  The store holds what the program wrote; that is what shared
  answers are made of.
- A law that HOLDS A BINDING TO ITS ANNOTATION compares the value to
  the DECLARED type it computed, never to the binding's own type —
  asking the binding for its type compares the value against itself,
  and the law silently stops refusing anything.
- Ask a BINDING, never a NAME, whether it is a const/a capture/a
  seat. A name may be defined twice (a `let` shadowing a const), so
  a name-keyed question and the binding in hand answer about
  DIFFERENT statements — the mismatch reads a slot nobody wrote
  ("index -1"). One question, asked of the statement. And a
  name-keyed table holds what it holds: `resolve_assign` asked
  `binding_of(name)`, a LOCALS table, so a fn's name walked
  through as a place — the walk had already recorded the root's
  binding; ask that.
- A BODY IS TYPED UNDER ITS SIGNATURE, so a declaration whose
  SIGNATURE WAS REFUSED has no scope for its body to be typed in —
  and the empty list that stands in for the missing one is read as
  a real scope by every seat. `walk_under` sets `self.scope =
  sig?.params ?? []`, the plausible default the protocol law
  refuses, and `target_type`'s `.Param(i) -> self.scope[i]` then
  indexed past the end: a generic METHOD is refused whole (F2031,
  no sig recorded) and its body still walks, so `fn f<T: Tr>(x: T)
  { x.m() }` inside an `impl` CRASHED THE COMPILER while the same
  fn at the top level was fine. The tell was a SIBLING PAIR
  disagreeing in one match — `.Receiver -> self.scope.first() ??
  self.error_type` was total and `.Param(i)` was not, four lines
  apart, so one seat kind had the guard and the other did not.
  SEVERAL SPELLINGS OF ONE QUESTION IS THE DEFECT, not the missing
  bound: every one asks "what type does seat i wear", and one file
  held five — two receiver reads, total, and three parameter reads,
  none of them. The split was invisible because each pair sat
  inside ONE match, arms apart, so a reader checking either arm saw
  a guard right beside it. There is one reader now (`seat_type`),
  and the refusal was already spoken before the body ran, which is
  what makes Error the honest answer rather than a defect voice.
- A COPIED TEMPLATE'S SPANS ARE ITS ORIGIN FILE'S OFFSETS — so its
  errors point home — and any pass that reads a span as THIS file's
  offset must ask `store.spanned_elsewhere(e)` first. `range_bodies`
  did not, and `within`'s copied nodes landed in whatever `client.av`
  declared at `time.av`'s offsets (a write through `self` blamed on
  `describe`). A sublanguage's nodes are foreign too but spanned HERE
  (shifted into the block); `ForeignRange.spanned_home` tells them apart.
- A READ WEARS THE TYPE OF WHAT IS READ, never the type of the node
  doing the reading. This bit THREE times in one slice: a captured
  callee took the CALL's type (a call's type is its answer, never its
  callee's), a capture took the LAMBDA's type (a lambda is a managed
  box, so an `int` capture looked managed and the memory pass
  retained a number), and a field read took the field expression's
  type where the SUBJECT's decides the layout. A register's recorded
  type is the wrong witness under mono, where it may still name a
  type parameter; the STATIC type of the thing being read is right.
- UNIFY BINDS, `accepts` RECORDS. `unify` agrees two types and pins a
  declaration's Vars; it does NOT record the lift that lowering
  mints. A seat that unifies and returns without passing through the
  agreement door silently drops the widen — invisible for as long as
  the widen happens to be identity, and a wrong answer the day the
  representation changes. The door is ONE verb, `agreed` (checks.av),
  and the three unified seats — a call argument, a struct field, an
  enum payload — call it; the payload once short-circuited and
  refused a `dyn` box and an auto-Ok its siblings took
  (compiler/tests/seats holds the proof).
- EVERY POINTER AVRA HOLDS CARRIES A HEADER. The runtime counts
  references in sixteen bytes BEFORE each payload (tag, kind, rc,
  and a LENGTH — a string's text length, a record's payload bytes),
  and `avra_rc_retain/release` read that header — so a managed
  value that came from anywhere else reads memory that is not ours.
  The sources are all headered: the backend's string constants
  (`avra_llvm_build_text`, kind STATIC, immortal),
  the runtime's own words (`avra_bool_text`, "null"), argv and the
  environment (`str_static`). A new C fn that answers TEXT to a
  program allocates it with `box_alloc`/`str_owned`, or
  `str_static` when the program must never own it — never a bare
  `malloc` or a C literal. The tag is the belt (`hdr` refuses a
  header without it, and an unaligned or null-page address before
  reading anything); the law is the braces. THE FLOOR IS THE NULL
  PAGE, NEVER THE IMAGE BASE: a 4 GB floor held only while the loader
  put everything high, so under valgrind (and any non-PIE image)
  every box read as foreign — nothing counted, nothing freed, every
  constant copied — and the first Linux profile reported that as the

- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness
